sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s tackle those sneaky mistakes that trip up even experienced coders when using if statements!

• How to spot the most common if-statement errors
• Why your code might not run as expected
• Simple fixes to make your logic bulletproof

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're a traffic light controller. If the light is red, cars stop. If it's green, they go. But what if you forget to handle yellow? Or worse - what if you mix up red and green? That’s exactly how if-statement errors feel!

Most if-statement mistakes fall into these categories:

• **Missing braces**: Like forgetting to close a door - your code might still run, but not how you intended
• **Logic errors**: The code runs, but gives wrong results (like saying 2+2=5)
• **Condition mistakes**: Using = instead of ==, or confusing && with ||

Here’s the golden rule: *Always test your if statements with different inputs* - especially edge cases!

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Always use == for comparisons, = for assignment
✓ Braces {} protect your code from logic errors
✓ Test with edge cases (0, negative numbers, empty strings)
✓ Indentation helps readability but doesn’t affect execution
✓ Boolean variables should have clear names (isAdult, hasPermission)

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use IDE warnings to catch = vs == errors
Test one condition at a time when debugging
donts: Don’t forget braces for multi-line if blocks
Don’t nest if statements too deeply (3 levels max)
sections.protip: Enable 'show whitespace' in your IDE to spot missing braces or semicolons instantly!

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 If-statement errors often come from small syntax mistakes with big consequences
📌 Always test with multiple inputs to catch logic errors
📌 Use == for comparisons, = for assignment - never mix them up!
📌 You're ready to write bulletproof selection statements!
